title: Tick removal
what: A doctor or nurse carefully pulls out the attached tick in one piece. The tick can be sent to a lab to test for infections.
why: When a tick has attached to your skin. The sooner it is removed, the lower the risk of infection.
duration: the removal itself takes a few minutes
tell_doctor: If you have had the tick-borne encephalitis vaccine
Where the tick bit you: in a forest, a field, and in what area

prepare.title: Do not pull
prepare.text: Do not put oil, cream, or alcohol on the tick, and do not twist it out with your fingers. This can make it release more saliva.

prepare.title: Act fast
prepare.text: Go to an urgent care center or clinic the same day. If there is no help nearby, the tick can be removed with tweezers or a thread.

prepare.title: If you removed it yourself
prepare.text: Put the tick in a small jar with a damp cotton ball and close the lid. Clean the bite with an antiseptic.

bring: The tick in a closed jar, if you already removed it
Your vaccination records, if you have them
steps: The tick is gripped with tweezers or a special hook right at the skin
It is pulled out slowly in one piece, without jerking
The wound is cleaned with an antiseptic
The tick is put in a jar. It can be sent for testing
The doctor decides if you need medicine to prevent infection
feel: Usually almost nothing, just a light pinch
after: If the tick was sent for testing, results usually take 1 to 3 days
Watch your health for 3 to 4 weeks and check your temperature
A little redness around the bite in the first days can happen
If a black dot is left in the skin, show it to a doctor
red_flags: Fever, headache, or body aches in the coming weeks: see a doctor right away and mention the tick
A red spot or ring around the bite that keeps growing
Fever with bleeding, bruises, or blood from the gums or nose: call emergency services right away

faq.q: What if the tick's head stays in the skin?
faq.a: Clean it with an antiseptic and show it to a doctor. It often comes out on its own. Do not dig it out with a needle.

faq.q: Should I send the tick for testing?
faq.a: It is useful. If an infection is found in the tick, the doctor can start prevention or treatment sooner.

faq.q: Can I remove a tick myself?
faq.a: Yes, with tweezers right at the skin, slowly and without jerking. Do not use oil or alcohol.
